newsitem.title: FRANCE: Airbus partners sign restructuring accord - paper.
newsitem.headline: Airbus partners sign restructuring accord - paper.

text.p: Partners in the Airbus consortium have signed an accord that will turn the plane maker into a corporation from its current partnership status by the end of 1999, a French newspaper reported on Monday.
Les Echos financial daily said the agreement, mapped out in preliminary form in early January, was signed at the weekend and would now go to the next Airbus board meeting on January 21.
Airbus was not immediately available for comment.
Partners in Airbus resolved last July to turn the consortium into a corporation to streamline decision-making and followed this up with the outlines of an accord earlier this month.
The restrucuturing plans took on a more urgent tone after Boeing and McDonnell Douglas said last month they would merge and form a civil and military giant with nearly $50 billion in annual sales.

Airbus is currently a Groupement d'Interet Economique (group of shared economic interests), a French legal entity which makes no profits or losses in its own right. Instead these go to the four partners who make decisions by consensus.
The four partners are French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace(DASA), and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA(CASA) of Spain.
Aerospatiale and DASA have 38 percent each. British Aerospace has 20 percent and CASA of Spain four percent.
